boardStatus: No single US board certifies a broad Endocrine Surgery subspecialty. ABS ACTPS FPD is an exam/Focused Practice Designation limited to adult complex thyroid and parathyroid surgery and is not a new board subspecialty certificate. ABS/ABOHNS co-developed its blueprint. ABS lists existing board certification, case/fellowship, license, participation and practice eligibility conditions. Verify candidate-specific current rules directly with ABS/ABOHNS. The AAES accredits comprehensive clinical fellowship programs; it does not issue an endocrine-surgery board certificate. AHNS program accreditation is training-program status, not a separate board credential. No separate ABS/ABOHNS exam is identified for adrenal, pancreatic/GI NET or whole-field endocrine surgery. Current pages checked 2026-10-07.
boardEligibilityNotice: This non-credit independent course does not make learners board-eligible, satisfy any prerequisite, or qualify them to sit any examination. General surgery/ENT residency completion, certification, licensure, case logs, fellowship accreditation and examination decisions are governed only by each responsible body.

boardStatus.notBoardEligible: No course completion, video hour, assessment score or case simulation supplies ABVLM pathway eligibility, supervised case counts, venous ultrasound logs, medical licensure, or credentialing.

boardEligibilityNotice: ABVLM’s February 2026 candidate handbook lists pathway-specific prerequisites, which include specified ACGME/RCPSC/AOA/other training, medical licensure, board status, CME, ultrasound logs and/or VLM case logs depending on pathway, plus its cognitive exam. Verify the current rules directly with ABVLM. This independent course cannot confer ACGME credit, licensure, eligibility, case-volume credit, procedural competence or certification; it cannot guarantee passing.

Current criteria require unrestricted licensure, primary ABIM/AOBIM board certification and qualifying fellowship or practice pathway. BWH says fellows are eligible for the exam but individual prerequisites still apply. PVI is a separate examination leading to the RPVI interpretation credential, not the specialty board. No separate ABIM vascular medicine subspecialty exam was established in the sources reviewed.
boardEligibilityNotice: This course grants no ABVM/RPVI eligibility. As checked 2026-10-07, ABVM requires unrestricted medical license, current ABIM/AOBIM primary certification, and a qualifying training pathway (including an eligible ≥12-month vascular medicine fellowship) or practice pathway. BWH invites physicians after accredited cardiovascular or pulmonary/critical-care fellowship; internal-medicine graduates may be individually considered. Verify current individual criteria with Inteleos/APCA and the programme.

boardNames: American Board of Surgery (ABS), Vascular Surgery primary certificate (Vascular Surgery Board administers examinations)
boardStatus: A distinct ABS primary certificate in Vascular Surgery exists. Initial certification requires an approved training pathway and successful completion of both the Vascular Surgery Qualifying Examination (VSQE) and Vascular Surgery Certifying Examination (VSCE). The VSQE is the cognitive examination; the VSCE is an oral clinical-reasoning examination. The reviewed sources do not identify a separate endovascular-surgery board examination or certification; endovascular care is within vascular surgery training and assessment.
boardEligibilityNotice: This independent educational curriculum confers no ABS/ABMS/ACGME status, board eligibility, licensure, operative privileges, procedural competence, credential, or guarantee of passing. ABS eligibility requires approved postgraduate training, documented supervised clinical experience and operative logs, and other current requirements. As checked 2026-10-07, the ABS lists 250 major vascular reconstructions, specified critical-care cases, ATLS plus ACLS/ALS for VSQE registration, RPVI certification and unrestricted U.S./Canadian medical licensure for VSCE registration; exact requirements can change. Independent/ESP candidates need an approved General Surgery QE application before VSQE access, but passing GSQE is not necessarily prerequisite to vascular certification. Consult ABS directly.

boardStatus.physicianSpecialtyStatus: Sports Medicine is a clinical subspecialty/CAQ, not a standalone physician residency specialty. Emergency Sports Medicine is the specific institutional fellowship label for a clinical EM-graduate track. It is not the same as a generic sports medicine directory category.
boardStatus.exam: Sports Medicine CAQ/ABEM SPM Certification Examination; ABFM develops/administers the examination, ABEM credentials eligible ABEM candidates.
boardStatus.programmeAccreditation: MGB says its one-year programme fulfills all ACGME requirements for Sports Medicine CAQ board eligibility. The official programme page reviewed did not expressly label the specific MGB programme ACGME-accredited; independent current accreditation verification was not obtained. ABEM eligibility requires completion of an ACGME-accredited programme, so the wording is not treated as proof of individual eligibility.

boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course does not confer board eligibility. The MGB page says the fellowship fulfills ACGME requirements for Sports Medicine CAQ eligibility. ABEM requires qualifying underlying certification, continuing certification, medical licensure and successful completion of an ACGME-accredited sports-medicine fellowship. Specific current site accreditation and an individual’s eligibility were not independently verified. Check with ABEM/ABFM and programme officials. Passing the examination is not guaranteed.

studyHours.plan: A transparent 12-week self-study plan at roughly 10 hours/week: 36 hours viewing counted external free video if completed; about 48 hours reading/annotation; about 24 hours case reasoning and assignment; about 12 hours retrieval practice and review. Verified media currently supplies only 2.5528 hours, so remaining planned viewing must be developed as original material and is not ready or counted. This plan is not official fellowship time.

boardNames: American Board of Dermatology (ABD) – Micrographic Dermatologic Surgery (MDS) subspecialty certification examination
boardStatus: An actual clinical physician subspecialty fellowship exists, with ACGME accreditation identified by official institutions and ABD. The American Board of Dermatology administers a separate MDS subspecialty certification exam/certificate; this is not a separate independent specialty board. ABD states that for 2026 onward, candidates must complete an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship; the prior practice pathway ended after 2025. No second separate MDS board examination was identified. General dermatology certification prerequisites and individual exam eligibility remain governed by ABD.
boardEligibilityNotice: This independent self-study course does not confer dermatology board certification, MDS eligibility, credentialing, or exam access. As of the ABD notice checked 2026-10-07, completion of an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship is required for the MDS exam beginning with the 2026 administration. ABD determines candidate-specific eligibility; verify current ABD rules.
